Subject: Re: Private deployment feasibility — control-plane & minimal network checklist

Folks — draft checklist below (short form) — happy to expand to a single-slide/netops handout.

Control-plane & network checklist (minimal):
- VPC CIDR(s) + intended subnets (app/docs: management, compute, storage)
- Control-plane endpoint model: customer-managed API LB (recommended) OR Redwood-managed control plane in customer VPC (requires entitlement).
- Allowed inbound ports to control plane: 443 (API), 9411 (metrics — optional), 22 (bastion — optional; we prefer ephemeral access).
- Outbound egress: allowed to our model repo endpoints and container registry (list of IPs/hostnames), NTP, and STS/KMS endpoints if using cloud KMS.
- TLS cert approach: customer-provided certs on LB OR Redwood-provisioned certs via ACME (customer approval required).
- Service account and IAM mappings: list of short-lived service principals we will need for telemetry/alarms.
- Network flow logs & retention window required for audit (we recommend 90 days minimum for pilot).
- NAT/egress policies: minimal — avoid broad open egress; we can provide exact hosts.

Attachment: controlplane-network-reqs.txt (short host/IP list + port table) — sending separately.

Resource implications (very rough):
- Pilot prep & onboarding: 2 SRE-days + 1 infra engineer-day (to validate networking and control-plane config).
- Pilot operations (two-week window): 1 on-call engineer (0.2 FTE across 2 weeks) + 4 hours/week of platform SME availability for troubleshooting.
- Runbook & delivery docs: 1 delivery PM ~2 days to produce run-of-show and sign-off checklist.

If they require Redwood-managed control plane in-customer VPC (we currently treat this as an exception path), add: ~2 additional infra engineer-days for entitlement and hardened config; ~1 additional SRE-day for initial support.

Karthik
Principal Architect | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment feasibility — pilot staffing & runbook strawman

Adding staffing and a proposed runbook outline. I attached a strawman pilot scope workbook (pilot-scope-strawman.xlsx).

Staffing (detailed estimate for a 2-week pilot):
- Onboarding week (week 0): 1 infra engineer (2 days), 1 delivery PM (3 days), 1 security engineer (1 day for questionnaire answers), 1 SRE (1 day) — total ~7 person-days.
- Pilot execution (weeks 1–2): 1 on-call SRE (rotating, ~0.2 FTE), platform SME 4 hours/week, delivery PM ~0.5 days/week for coordination.
- Post-pilot wrap (1 week): 1 infra engineer (1 day) + PM (1 day) + security engineer (0.5 day) for artifacts and lessons.

Estimated total: ~14–18 person-days across 3 weeks (conservative). If Greenbank wants Redwood-managed control plane, add 5–7 person-days for entitlement and hardened config.

Runbook outline (short):
1) Pre-kick checklist (network details, certs, service accounts)
2) Day 0 — deploy control plane (validation steps)
3) Day 1 — smoke tests, sample inference traffic, metrics sanity
4) Day 2–14 — run traffic, collect latency/cost metrics, daily 30-minute sync w/ customer
5) Escalation matrix & rollbacks (include automatic fallback to hosted endpoint if service degrades)
6) Post-pilot deliverables: audit logs extract, runbook, list of regression checks

Attachments: pilot-scope-strawman.xlsx (workbook with roles & timeline)

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Delivery | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment feasibility — SOC2 evidence & gating items

Sam — quick list of SOC2 / compliance evidence Greenbank typically asks for (we can produce these during pilot):
- SOC2 Type II report (redacted) + scope explanation (what hosted components are in scope)
- Data flow diagram showing control plane vs. runtime (we'll annotate with where logs are retained in-customer VPC)
- Audit log export instructions (how to extract S3 logs or VPC flow logs)
- KMS integration docs (if they plan to use customer KMS/HSM)
- Retention and deletion policy for ephemeral KV caches and model artifacts

Gating: if they require 365+ day retention or on-site auditors, we should treat as a separate project and add to timeline/cost. For pilot, recommend 90-day retention and remote evidence exchange.

I'll start assembling a one-page evidence pack and link in the Drive folder.

Jonas Weber
